reference: GNU coreutils split(1), run under system Bash with the harness reference PATH; parity compares status, stdout, and complete private fixture trees including bytes and modes. Bash type/help metadata contracts use Bash builtins and the generated short-help description pinned in config/bash-loadables.list.
coverage: Default stdin input and xaa prefix naming
Line chunk boundaries, a one-character suffix, and an unterminated final record
Byte chunk boundaries over NUL and high-bit bytes, including an exact multiple with no empty trailing piece
The 1k byte-size suffix at the 1024-byte boundary
Two redirected stdin invocations in one shell
Truncation of an existing piece and umask-derived modes for a new piece
Bash builtin type and generated short-help metadata
exclusions: This is focused coverage, not the full GNU split option surface; numeric line/byte splitting and common suffix behavior are covered, while options such as --number, --filter, and --elide-empty-files are outside the documented builtin interface.
No host/device paths, write-failure devices, or input aliasing cases are used.

cases.purpose: With no input or prefix operand, split reads stdin and creates the default xaa piece.
Split five records into two-line pieces, use a one-character suffix, and preserve the final unterminated record.
Byte splitting must preserve NUL and high-bit bytes and must not create an empty piece when the input length is an exact multiple of the chunk size.
The 1k byte-size suffix denotes 1024 bytes: a 1025-byte fixture should produce one full piece and one one-byte piece.
Two split invocations in one shell consume separate redirected stdin streams, first by lines and then by bytes.
cases.script:
printf 'a
b
c
' > first; printf '\000xyz' > second; split -l 2 - first_ < first; split -b 2 - second_ < second

cases.purpose: An existing first piece is truncated rather than appended, its existing mode remains, and a newly created second piece follows the active umask.
cases.script:
printf 'fresh
next
' > input; umask 077; printf 'old data that must be truncated
' > itemaa; split -l 1 input item

cases.purpose: If the first output name is an existing directory, split reports a write/open failure and leaves the directory and input fixture intact.
cases.script: printf 'content\n' > input; mkdir pieceaa; split -l 1 input piece

cases.purpose: A zero line count is invalid; GNU status and candidate status are both asserted against the reference, and no output piece should be created.
Bash type metadata identifies the statically provided split command as a builtin, independently of PATH lookup.
Bash short help reports the supported split command synopsis.
